articles.title: 【一融双高】学校举办“一融双高”基层党建工作坊暨2025—2026年基层党建专项督导会 - 大连理工大学新闻网
articles.summary: 【一融双高】学校举办“一融双高”基层党建工作坊暨2025—2026年基层党建专项督导会 大连理工大学新闻网
articles.full_body:
Title: 【一融双高】学校举办“一融双高”基层党建工作坊暨2025—2026年基层党建专项督导会-大连理工大学新闻网

URL Source: https://news.google.com/rss/articles/CBMiWEFVX3lxTE12U283Nnd1NDdjWVVOS3NPYnRrckFTcUlhMnZxV3ozcjh0SDh4NFlrbENpVFNsbjJMNVhnMXBPMlVnNVNSeGp1dWRxd3JqMk94ZGlLM0czek8

Markdown Content:
为深入学习贯彻习近平党建思想，压紧压实基层党建工作责任，推动各二级党组织全面落细落实基层党建各项任务，持续提升党建工作质量与实效，7月24日，由学校党委组织部主办、生物工程学院承办的大连理工大学“一融双高”基层党建工作坊暨2025—2026年基层党建专项督导会在知微楼116报告厅举行。会议采用“集中培训+分组现场查阅资料”相结合的方式进行，学校特邀基层党建组织员列席指导，各二级党组织分管党建工作副职、专兼职组织员参会。

![Image 1](https://news.dlut.edu.cn/virtual_attach_file.vsb?afc=/o7nK2UmG8L7WkUOz7YL4C4Lm7DolWx7nlL8M49aM8M7L4-0gihFp2hmCIa0USysMSyPUSh2L4VkLNMRU4vYnNUbM7CDnzUDUzf2M7rkM4VFMmvbLl7ZnR6FLmr2nRNJqjfjo4OeoDnOp26N_dAs6YhXptQ0g47aLm-0LzUZLz9igtA8pUJcc&oid=1819948287&tid=1022&nid=148185&e=.jpg)

会议由生物工程学院党委副书记兼副院长李明智主持，生物工程学院党委书记杨君受邀致辞。会上，党委组织部副部长庞源传达全国党建工作座谈会精神、部署学校学习贯彻习近平党建思想有关要求，并就暑假期间开展树立和践行正确政绩观学习教育要求进行提示。党委巡视办公室专职巡视组组长郈兵作专题培训，培训坚持“问题导向”，聚焦本轮校内巡视中发现的基层党建领域重点问题，剖析深层次原因，进一步明确了工作规范和要求。

![Image 2](https://news.dlut.edu.cn/virtual_attach_file.vsb?afc=/UzvK8nNWkMmUYMON74M8lYn77YLmLx4LllPL7lanm9YLNU0gihFp2hmCIa0nkh2nSyDU1hfMmvao7-YLRNbnlC4L7lbMzM7nlnVnzC4oz6FUmN8L8WkU4MFnlVfn1b/v2veo4OeQ2POQDnZ_d6sgDTJQty0LzGYL1yPMR9PoRlJqdJnx&oid=1819948287&tid=1022&nid=148185&e=.jpg)

在基层党建督导环节，设立“两个议事规则”执行、“三会一课”和主题党日开展、发展党员工作、学习教育和党员干部教育培训四个专项工作组，分别由党委组织部和党委巡视办公室相关负责人担任组长，对2025年7月至2026年6月期间的基层党建工作落实情况进行现场督导检查。各工作组按照前期工作部署，对照《基层党建督导对照检查清单》，逐项核实材料，现场查阅会议纪要、党员档案、培训记录等，详细记录并分类整理检查中发现的具体问题和共性问题，同时交流经验做法，促进互学互鉴。

![Image 3](https://news.dlut.edu.cn/virtual_attach_file.vsb?afc=/MRNKbU4-PMRMfoOlUbUzU4L8LDL4-xaMRWRoz6VU4CDMl-0gihFp2hmCIa0nSh7MkyaU1yaUzffo7r2MRfRLNlZnmfknmf2UzTfLN-PM4MFMlVfnzWknRWFLml8MllJqjfjo4OeoDnOp26N_dAs6YhXptQ0g47aLm-0LzUZLz9igtA8pUJcc&oid=1819948287&tid=1022&nid=148185&e=.jpg)

本次专项督导工作既是对各二级党组织党建工作的一次全面“体检”，也是深化“一融双高”建设、推动巡视整改任务落地见效的重要举措。通过基层党建督导，精准掌握各二级党组织党建工作情况，进一步压实了基层党建工作主体责任，明确了下一步改进方向。全校各二级党组织将以此为契机，坚持以习近平党建思想为统领，树牢大抓基层的鲜明导向，针对督导反馈问题制定整改方案并严格落实，将整改同深化“一融双高”建设相结合，同落实全面从严治党主体责任相结合，为学校“加速卓越”、实现“1510”发展目标提供坚强组织保障。

articles.full_body:
Title: In Diary, Fauci Bragged of Role in School Closures. At Hearing, He Took the 5th

URL Source: https://www.the74million.org/article/in-diary-fauci-bragged-of-role-in-school-closures-at-hearing-he-took-the-5th

Published Time: 2026-07-29T16:44:09-04:00

Markdown Content:
_Get stories like this delivered straight to your inbox._[**Sign up for The 74 Newsletter**](https://www.the74million.org/about/newsletters/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=top&utm_id=newsletter)

In a three-hour hearing Wednesday, Dr. Anthony Fauci, the influential scientist who led the national response to COVID, refused to respond to questions about his role in school closures and the mask and social distancing guidelines that experts say have drastically set back students’ learning.

Subpoenaed by Sen. Rand Paul of Kentucky, the Republican chair of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, Fauci repeatedly invoked his Fifth Amendment right to decline to respond, and accused the senator of an “unhinged obsession” with putting him in jail. Former President Joe Biden [pardoned Fauci](https://www.justice.gov/pardon/media/1385746/dl?inline) for any crimes he may have committed dating back to 2014 in his official roles with the government, but Paul threatened “repercussions” over Fauci’s refusal to answer questions and said the committee will vote next week on contempt charges.

“You argue that you did not personally issue every lockdown order, close schools or impose every mandate, but officials across the country invoked your authority to justify these decisions,” said Paul, who described Fauci as more concerned about his celebrity status than scientific evidence. “Children lost years of education.”

The hearing followed Paul’s recent release of [a journal](https://www.paul.senate.gov/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/2026.07.24_Tonys-Diary-Package.pdf) Fauci kept during the height of the COVID crisis. The entries reveal his conflict with President Donald Trump over keeping schools open and his sense of pride that officials, like former New York City Mayor Bill de Blasio and California Gov. Gavin Newsom’s chief of staff followed his guidance on closing schools. On June 29, 2020, for example, he noted [a conversation](https://www.wbtv.com/2020/08/17/dr-fauci-told-nc-leaders-wait-before-reopening-schools-with-fully-in-person-learning/) with former North Carolina Gov. Roy Cooper, a Democrat, about allowing in-person learning to resume that fall. “Since this is the first decision among governors regarding opening for the fall term, he feels that he will be the example,” Fauci wrote. “I recommended that he delay decision for two weeks.”

Democrats praised Fauci for his decades of service under both Republican and Democratic presidents and characterized the hearing as a personal vendetta by Paul. [Michigan Sen. Gary Peters](https://thehill.com/homenews/senate/5996425-gary-peters-rand-paul-anthony-fauci-covid-hearing/), the ranking Democrat on the committee, said the hearing was a distraction from some of the current public health issues facing the public, including a rise in measles cases. With staff cuts, he added, “the administration has hollowed out the public health workforce.”

Republicans, he said, are just “relitigating the past.”

![Image 1](https://www.the74million.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/sen-rand-paul-fauci-750x500.jpg)

Sen. Rand Paul, a Kentucky Republican and chair of the Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee, tried to get Dr. Anthony Fauci to apologize to the nation, but Fauci refused to answer questions. (Alex WROBLEWSKI / AFP via Getty Images)

Much of the questioning focused on whether Fauci misled the public about the source of the virus, saying that it originated in a Chinese market, while he wrote to himself that the market was only an “amplifier.” Since 2021, Paul has accused Fauci of lying about the National Institutes of Health funding the type of lab research in China that created COVID.

“Many people would say, ‘Well gosh, that doesn’t sound like a really good idea, to create viruses that don’t exist in nature to see if they’ll infect human cells,’ ” Paul said. “The American people deserve an apology.”

### **‘Slower in learning’**

The nation’s schools shut down in mid-March 2020 as states responded to calls from Trump, under Fauci’s advice, to “slow the spread” of the disease. But what most assumed would be short-term measures turned into more than a year of on-again, off-again closures and intense battles over mask and vaccine mandates. By October of 2020, education researchers began to estimate that students had [lost more than a year](https://www.the74million.org/article/students-could-have-lost-as-much-as-183-days-of-learning-time-in-reading-232-days-in-math-during-first-four-months-of-largely-virtual-schooling/) of learning in reading and math.

Those predictions held up. Data from the most recent [National Assessment of Educational Progress](https://www.nagb.gov/powered-by-naep/the-2024-nations-report-card/10-takeaways-from-2024-naep-results.html) shows that overall, students still haven’t reached pre-pandemic levels in reading and math.

Children are “slower in learning language now because they couldn’t watch someone’s lips moving,” said Oklahoma Sen. James Lankford, a Republican.

He also pressed Fauci on a May 6, 2020 conversation he had with Dr. Robert Redfield, former director of the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, over the fact that 1 million children had missed their measles vaccinations because of the shutdown.

“This is terrible and needs to be addressed since on that basis alone, there would be far, far more excess deaths from measles among children than coronavirus deaths among children,” Fauci wrote.

But Sen. Maggie Hassan, a New Hampshire Democrat, blamed the current administration for the rise in measles cases. So far this year,there have been over 2,300 reported measles cases, [according to the CDC](https://www.cdc.gov/measles/data-research/index.html).

“Children are dying because there has been increased vaccine hesitancy fueled by Robert F. Kennedy,” Hassan said about the Health and Human Services secretary.

During the hearing, Trump took credit [on social media](https://truthsocial.com/@realDonaldTrump/posts/117003098657536803) for the rapid development of the COVID vaccine. But he said he relied less on Fauci’s advice over time.

“I didn’t let him shut the country down, although he wanted to,” Trump wrote. “I went the Federalist way, and let the governors decide.”

The public, however, thought the president didn’t respond quickly enough to the outbreak. In an April 2020 [Pew Research Center survey](https://www.pewresearch.org/politics/2020/04/16/most-americans-say-trump-was-too-slow-in-initial-response-to-coronavirus-threat/), 65% of Americans said Trump was too slow to take major steps to address the threat.

articles.full_body:
Title: New Staffing Models Put Strong Teachers Out Front

URL Source: https://www.the74million.org/article/new-staffing-models-put-strong-teachers-out-front

Published Time: 2026-07-29T12:30:00-04:00

Markdown Content:
_Get stories like this delivered straight to your inbox._[**Sign up for The 74 Newsletter**](https://www.the74million.org/about/newsletters/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=top&utm_id=newsletter)

In Carlsbad, N.M., a tiny district in the southeastern corner of the state, nine of its 12 schools have turned teacher assignments upside-down, inviting their best teachers to coach a team of colleagues, model lessons and take direct responsibility for the achievement of every student the team serves.

In exchange, each teacher-leader earns substantially more — without leaving the classroom.

The idea grew out of an emerging staffing model called [Opportunity Culture](https://www.opportunityculture.org/), now in its fourth year in the Carlsbad Municipal School District. It’s reshaping how schools there and elsewhere deploy teachers.

Part of a broader movement sometimes called [strategic staffing](https://workforce.education.asu.edu/strategic-staffing/), its premise is simple: Instead of assuming that every classroom needs its own solitary teacher, with skills roughly equal to the person in the next room, schools identify teachers with a track record of strong student growth, putting them in charge of a large group of students or educators — or both.

In one model, a “core team” of two to six skilled teachers — at least one of whom is a special education teacher — teach classes of 50 to 100 students, with assistance from aides and volunteers.

![Image 1](https://www.the74million.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Allison-Hervol-headshot-1.jpg)

Allison Hervol

Since Opportunity Culture emerged more than a decade ago, it has spread to more than [1,150 schools across 18 states](https://www.opportunityculture.org/opportunity-culture-stats/). At its core is a teacher known as a Multi-Classroom Leader or MCL — a master teacher who takes on formal responsibility for coaching up to eight colleagues while keeping their own classroom. They get a bump in salary that can be significant, said Allison Hervol, who oversees curriculum and instruction for Carlsbad. “Some of our MCLs make close to, if not more than, what their principal makes,” she said.

The key is that these teachers aren’t pulled out of the classroom entirely. An MCL coaching three teachers might still teach for four hours a day. That avoids creating teacher vacancies in an already tight labor market.

![Image 2](https://www.the74million.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/Bryan-Hassel-2-1.jpg)

Bryan Hassel

The structure grew out of a model developed by the North Carolina-based nonprofit [Public Impact](https://publicimpact.com/) around 2013, but it has only recently earned wider attention. Before 2013, Public Impact was “a multi-topic consulting and research organization,” said [Bryan Hassel](https://publicimpact.com/our-team/bryan-hassel/), the organization’s co-president. It soon pivoted to trying to optimize teacher roles, time and pay.

[Lennon Audrain](https://search.asu.edu/profile/3051803), an assistant professor and Head of Innovation and Policy Initiatives at Arizona State University, is careful to note that the idea of strategic staffing isn’t actually new, pointing to team-teaching experiments dating to the 1960s and ’70s, when districts short on trained staff began recruiting “homeroom moms” to help manage classroom data — a role that eventually evolved into the modern [paraeducator](https://study.com/academy/lesson/video/what-is-a-paraeducator.html).

![Image 3](https://www.the74million.org/wp-content/uploads/2026/07/lennon-audrain-300x300-1.jpg)

Lennon Audrain

What is new, he said, is the technology available to make those teams work well: tools for grouping students, tracking data and designing roles that didn’t exist 40 or 50 years ago

[ASU’s version](https://workforce.education.asu.edu/blog/a-federal-investment-in-strategic-school-staffing/) of strategic staffing insists on at least two certified educators at the core of a team, with paraeducators, community members or part-time teachers added as needed. Most importantly, he said, staffing decisions must map directly onto a school’s actual instructional priorities: If a school wants to raise math achievement, for instance, it should build math teams.

While it seems self-evident, he said, the key is to have priorities in the first place.

### **‘A mentor teacher isn’t anything new’**

In December 2023, the consulting firm [Education First](https://www.education-first.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/12/EducationFirst_StrategicSchoolStaffingLandscapeScan.pdf), which helped popularize new teacher models, laid out the pressures pushing schools toward them. On the student side, it pointed to steep pandemic-era drops in NAEP scores, including an eight-point decline in eighth-grade reading between 2019 and 2022.

On the staffing side, it found that teachers were earning about 24% less than similarly educated peers, with nearly one in five working a second job. Giving effective teachers more pay, more influence and a better reason to stick around, it concluded, could help solve both problems.

By then, Opportunity Culture had already reached more than 800 schools, encompassing over 5,400 teachers and 150,000 students. The data also suggested that the model could turn average teachers into excellent — or nearly excellent — ones.

And it proved popular with teachers: 97% of MCLs and 87% of teammates wanted to keep using Opportunity Culture the following year.

MCLs earn roughly 20% above typical teacher pay, according to Public Impact’s Hassel.

The model has grown well beyond a handful of pilot districts: Charlotte-Mecklenburg Schools in North Carolina now runs it in 179 schools, amounting to nearly every building.

Carlsbad’s Hervol said keeping proven teachers in the classroom not only preserves their direct impact on students — it also builds trust among teachers, who would rather be coached by a colleague than a trainer from central office.

The district also paired the rollout with Doug Lemov’s [Teach Like a Champion](https://teachlikeachampion.org/) framework, with teachers retaining freedom over their own rooms.

The results, Hervol said, have been hard to ignore. At one elementary school, fourth-grade reading proficiency climbed from around 35% to 68%, with higher scores at “almost all of our campuses” that have implemented the Opportunity Culture framework.

In North Carolina, which a decade ago began piloting a teacher-leader program, 76% of participating schools showed higher growth scores on state tests, compared to 45% of comparison schools. And teacher turnover dropped to just 1% to 3% in the pilot schools, compared with 7.5% to 9% statewide.

### **‘It’s really working’**

为深入学习贯彻习近平党建思想，压紧压实基层党建工作责任，推动各二级党组织全面落细落实基层党建各项任务，持续提升党建工作质量与实效，7月24日，由学校党委组织部主办、生物工程学院承办的大连理工大学“一融双高”基层党建工作坊暨2025—2026年基层党建专项督导会在知微楼116报告厅举行。会议采用“集中培训+分组现场查阅资料”相结合的方式进行，学校特邀基层党建组织员列席指导，各二级党组织分管党建工作副职、专兼职组织员参会。

会议由生物工程学院党委副书记兼副院长李明智主持，生物工程学院党委书记杨君受邀致辞。会上，党委组织部副部长庞源传达全国党建工作座谈会精神、部署学校学习贯彻习近平党建思想有关要求，并就暑假期间开展树立和践行正确政绩观学习教育要求进行提示。党委巡视办公室专职巡视组组长郈兵作专题培训，培训坚持“问题导向”，聚焦本轮校内巡视中发现的基层党建领域重点问题，剖析深层次原因，进一步明确了工作规范和要求。

![Image 2](https://news.dlut.edu.cn/virtual_attach_file.vsb?afc=/UzvK8nNWkMmUYMON74M8lYn77YLmLx4LllPL7lanm9YLNU0gihFp2hmCIa0nkh2nSyDU1hfMmvao7-YLRNbnlC4L7lbMzM7nlnVnzC4oz6FUmN8L8WkU4MFnlVfn1b/v2veo4OeQ2POQDnZ_d6sgDTJQty0LzGYL1yPMR9PoRlJqdJnx&oid=1819948287&tid=1022&nid=148185&e=.jpg)

在基层党建督导环节，设立“两个议事规则”执行、“三会一课”和主题党日开展、发展党员工作、学习教育和党员干部教育培训四个专项工作组，分别由党委组织部和党委巡视办公室相关负责人担任组长，对2025年7月至2026年6月期间的基层党建工作落实情况进行现场督导检查。各工作组按照前期工作部署，对照《基层党建督导对照检查清单》，逐项核实材料，现场查阅会议纪要、党员档案、培训记录等，详细记录并分类整理检查中发现的具体问题和共性问题，同时交流经验做法，促进互学互鉴。

![Image 3](https://news.dlut.edu.cn/virtual_attach_file.vsb?afc=/MRNKbU4-PMRMfoOlUbUzU4L8LDL4-xaMRWRoz6VU4CDMl-0gihFp2hmCIa0nSh7MkyaU1yaUzffo7r2MRfRLNlZnmfknmf2UzTfLN-PM4MFMlVfnzWknRWFLml8MllJqjfjo4OeoDnOp26N_dAs6YhXptQ0g47aLm-0LzUZLz9igtA8pUJcc&oid=1819948287&tid=1022&nid=148185&e=.jpg)

本次专项督导工作既是对各二级党组织党建工作的一次全面“体检”，也是深化“一融双高”建设、推动巡视整改任务落地见效的重要举措。通过基层党建督导，精准掌握各二级党组织党建工作情况，进一步压实了基层党建工作主体责任，明确了下一步改进方向。全校各二级党组织将以此为契机，坚持以习近平党建思想为统领，树牢大抓基层的鲜明导向，针对督导反馈问题制定整改方案并严格落实，将整改同深化“一融双高”建设相结合，同落实全面从严治党主体责任相结合，为学校“加速卓越”、实现“1510”发展目标提供坚强组织保障。

fact_packs.headline: New Staffing Models Put Strong Teachers Out Front
facts: Title: New Staffing Models Put Strong Teachers Out Front

_Get stories like this delivered straight to your inbox._[**Sign up for The 74 Newsletter**](https://www.the74million.org/about/newsletters/?utm_source=website&utm_medium=article&utm_campaign=top&utm_id=newsletter)

In Carlsbad, N.M., a tiny district in the southeastern corner of the state, nine of its 12 schools have turned teacher assignments upside-down, inviting their best teachers to coach a team of colleagues, model lessons and take direct responsibility for the achievement of every student the team serves.
In exchange, each teacher-leader earns substantially more — without leaving the classroom.

The idea grew out of an emerging staffing model called [Opportunity Culture](https://www.opportunityculture.org/), now in its fourth year in the Carlsbad Municipal School District. It’s reshaping how schools there and elsewhere deploy teachers.

Part of a broader movement sometimes called [strategic staffing](https://workforce.education.asu.edu/strategic-staffing/), its premise is simple: Instead of assuming that every classroom needs its own solitary teacher, with skills roughly equal to the person in the next room, schools identify teachers with a track record of strong student growth, putting them in charge of a large group of students or educators — or both.
In one model, a “core team” of two to six skilled teachers — at least one of whom is a special education teacher — teach classes of 50 to 100 students, with assistance from aides and volunteers.
